newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - stuffing knocked out by crude.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - stuffing knocked out by crude.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were pulled lower by falling crude on Tuesday.
Gasoline was easy although the downside was not as drastic as the $10-12 per tonne losses in NWE with strike-slowed French refinery production providing a brake, traders said.
Tight Italian supplies after Elf scooped up Med material last week also continued to underpin prices, they said.

Traders said the combination of an end to the last week's Elf refinery strike and weaker U.S. markets had tipped the balance in Europe, but said today's one day strike at some French refiners may still have some repurcussions.
Naphtha was easier with crude with little end user demand.
Traders said recently supportive North American buying had thinned with higher freight costs limiting arb opportunities.

Gas oil was pulled $2.50 lower by futures. Heating oil premiums were again under pressure from persistent length. One seller offered a cargo of Russian heating oil at cif high flat basis Genoa but found no bids and at least four other Russians were on offer.
Interest emerged for a combi cargo for 10,000 tonnes of gasoline and 20,000 tonnes into France and a combi of heating oil and jet fuel into Tunisia.
Traders explored an arb to Asia but sharp movements either side of a $30 differential complicated trade. Premiums low sulphur diesel Algerian grade were at around fob Med high +$3 basis Italy.

High sulphur fuel was besieged by weaker crude, but dealers said news that Romania had secured a $160m loan to buy 1.3 million tonnes this winter would give support. U.S material was understood to be heading into Romania. Fuel levels held steady around $108 fob. "The Med came off before NWE, so there was less far to fall," commented one trader. A low sulphur cargo was thought sold into the Med ex-NWE, but it was not confirmed.
